question: A cubical block of wood of side 14 cm is surmounted by a hemisphere of the largest possible diameter. What is the total surface area (in {cm}² ) of the solid thus formed? ({Use } pi = (22)/(7))
solution:
**Given:**

Side of the cubical block = 14 cm

Diameter of the hemisphere = Side of the cube = 14 cm

Radius of the hemisphere = Diameter/2 = 14/2 = 7 cm

**Formula used:**

1. Surface area of a cube = 6 × (Side)²

2. Curved surface area of a hemisphere = 2 × π × (Radius)²

3. Total surface area of the solid = Surface area of the cube + Curved surface area of the hemisphere - Area of the base of the hemisphere

Area of the base of the hemisphere = π × (Radius)²

**Calculation:**

Surface area of the cube = 6 × (14)²

⇒ 6 × 196 = 1176 cm²

Curved surface area of the hemisphere = 2 × (22/7) × (7)²

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 49 = 308 cm²

Area of the base of the hemisphere = (22/7) × (7)²

⇒ (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm²

Total surface area = Surface area of the cube + Curved surface area of the hemisphere - Area of the base of the hemisphere

⇒ 1176 + 308 - 154

⇒ 1330 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**
